extracted.intended_audience: children's book authors and illustrators, SCBWI members, publishers, and general readers interested in the award
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators (SCBWI) Golden Kite Awards: who is eligible, which categories are recognized, how winners/honors are chosen, prize amounts, and timing relative to publication. Useful for authors/illustrators considering submission or researching the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (membership and submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible books must be written or illustrated by SCBWI members, and submitted either by publishers or individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only works by SCBWI members may be considered; submissions may be made by the publisher or by individual (presumably the author/illustrator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The award currently recognizes literature in seven categories: "Young Reader and Middle Grade Fiction, Young Adult Fiction, Nonfiction Text for Young Readers, Nonfiction text for Older Readers, Picture Book Text, Picture Book Illustration, and Illustration for Older Readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be entered into the appropriate category matching the book's audience and format. (The article lists these as the categories current to the award.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging: peer jury composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are chosen by a panel of judges consisting of children’s book writers and illustrators. The Golden Kite Awards are the only children’s literary award judged by a jury of peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is performed by fellow practitioners (writers and illustrators), indicating peer assessment rather than e.g., critic or public voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor recipients named by judges
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the Golden Kite Award winners, honor book recipients are named by the judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges may designate additional honor books (runners-up) in each category; these honors are explicitly part of the judges' outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner and honor monetary awards and donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2006, each category's winner wins a $2,500 grant cash prize, as well as $1,000 to donate to their chosen non-profit organization. Honor winners receive $500, as well as $250 to donate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary amounts and donation allocations are specified and have been in effect since 2006; use this for understanding prize value and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sid Fleischman Award (humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2003, the Sid Fleischman Award for excellence in humorous writing is given in conjunction with the Golden Kite Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a separate, associated award presented alongside the Golden Kite Awards specifically recognizing humorous writing for children/young readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: award year relative to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: In the winners table, the year represents the year the awards were given, which is the year following publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting award-year listings, note that an award year (e.g., 2000) corresponds to books published the previous year (e.g., 1999).
